sections.h2: What a quitclaim deed is, and where it fits
sections.html:
A quitclaim deed is one of several deed types the county clerk records in Texas, alongside general warranty, special warranty, trustee's, sheriff's and tax deeds. It is filed in the deed records at the clerk's office covering the land.

A quitclaim passes whatever interest the signer has, if any, and promises nothing more. How much comfort that gives a buyer is a question for a title company or a Texas real estate attorney, so ask before you rely on anyone's promise about it.

For a seller the practical point is simple. A buyer's title company reads every deed in the chain, and a quitclaim anywhere in that chain can prompt extra questions. The sooner you know what is in your own chain of title, the fewer surprises appear after you sign a sale contract.

sections.h2: What else the county clerk handles
sections.html:
The clerk's office does several jobs that touch a sale. It is the county recorder for deeds, deeds of trust, liens and notices of foreclosure sale, the clerk of the commissioners court, and the office that takes probate filings such as applications and small estate affidavits.

One phone call can tell you whether a deed, a lien or a probate filing is on record against your property. State tax liens are filed there too: the Comptroller files notice with the county clerk, who records it in the state tax lien book. Request copies of whatever is indexed under your name and the prior owner's before you tell a buyer the title is clean.

  • Deed records for every type of conveyance named above.
  • Releases of liens, leases, sale contracts and powers of attorney.
  • Probate filings and small estate affidavits.

sections.h2: What a deed needs before the clerk will record it
sections.html:
The grantor signs, and the deed then needs either an acknowledgment before an officer who can take one, a sworn statement, or the signatures of two subscribing witnesses. This is the rule in Property Code 12.001(b). A notary, a county clerk, a district clerk or a county court judge can take an acknowledgment.

  • Signature by the person giving up the interest.
  • An acknowledgment or sworn statement, or two subscribing witnesses.
  • Filing in the clerk's office for the county that covers the land.
  • The recording fees the clerk charges, listed below.

Recording is how the public record shows who holds an interest. A deed that stays in a drawer does not appear in the clerk's records, and a later buyer or lender searching those records will not see it.

sections.h2: What the clerk charges to file a deed
sections.html:
The 2023 schedule has a small base charge per page plus several smaller add-ons. Your clerk's posted schedule controls, so phone the office before you file.

Recording fee items, 2023 county clerk schedule
Recording fee itemAmount
First pageFive dollars
Each added page or attachmentFour dollars
Each name over five to be indexed$0.25
Records management and preservation feeNot more than $10
Records archive feeNot more than $10
Records technology and infrastructure fee$2.00

A missing mailing address for the grantee can add $25.

sections.h2: Can a quitclaim deed move a house out of an estate?
sections.html:
Usually the route out of an estate runs through the probate paperwork, and a quitclaim signed by one heir does not replace it. Which papers go on record depends on how the owner left the property.

  • A recorded affidavit of death and a death certificate go with a transfer on death deed.
  • An estate under administration uses a deed from its executor or administrator.
  • A will proved as a muniment of title relies on the court order.
  • Without any of those, an affidavit of heirship may be used.

The county cannot add heirs to the old deed. Whoever inherits can ask the clerk what the records show. A sworn affidavit of heirship carries no court verification, and no law forces third parties to accept it.

sections.h2: Transfer on death deeds and Lady Bird deeds
sections.html:
Owners often ask about these as an alternative to handing a relative a quitclaim. A transfer on death deed passes real property without probate, can name charities as beneficiaries, can be cancelled by the owner, and must be on record at the clerk's office before the owner dies.

The Lady Bird deed, an enhanced life estate deed, lets the owner sell or mortgage without the beneficiary's consent. No official form exists for it. Because these deeds shape what a buyer can purchase later, a title company usually wants to see them before closing.

sections.h2: Taxes and liens that travel with a deed
sections.html:
Each January 1 a lien attaches to secure that year's property taxes, and it lets a court foreclose even after the title changes hands. Whoever held title on that date owes the year's bill and can be sued for it after selling.

Delinquent taxes block clean title for a buyer. Giving the house away by quitclaim does not wipe out that lien, so the tax office should confirm each year's status before any listing or transfer.

sections.h2: Selling a house you hold by quitclaim
sections.html:
Order a title search or call a title company early, and read each deed in your chain of title. Quitclaims, handwritten deeds, missing signatures and unrecorded transfers are the items that slow a closing.

  • Pull the recorded deeds from the county clerk and check each one for a signature and an acknowledgment.
  • Check whether every co-owner or heir signed.
  • Get a tax status statement for every year from the county tax office.
  • Find out from the title company what it requires before it will insure a buyer.

If the chain has gaps that the title company cannot clear, a Texas real estate attorney can say whether a corrective instrument or a court action is the right fix. A cash buyer will still want the chain to read cleanly, though with no lender in the deal the closing is often quicker once the gaps are repaired.

faqs.q: Is a quitclaim deed filed at the clerk's office in Texas?
faqs.a: Yes. Quitclaim deeds are recorded in the deed records at the clerk covering the real property, after the deed is signed and acknowledged or witnessed.

faqs.q: What does recording a Texas deed cost?
faqs.a: The 2023 schedule itemizes a charge per page, two records fees capped at $10 each and a $2.00 technology fee. Your clerk can quote the current total.

faqs.q: Can a quitclaim deed stop probate?
faqs.a: No. Inherited real property moves through a transfer on death deed, a muniment of title, an administered-estate deed or an affidavit of heirship. Ask the clerk or a probate attorney before relying on a quitclaim.

faqs.q: Will a quitclaim erase unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: No. The January 1 tax lien lets a court foreclose even after ownership changes, and a buyer cannot get clear title until delinquent taxes are paid.

faqs.q: Who can say whether my quitclaim will pass title insurance?
faqs.a: A title company or a Texas attorney. Each underwriter has its own requirements, so ask before you list.
